issues.t: Connecting rod bearings can fail and ruin the engine (recall)
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine that gets louder, an oil pressure warning, loss of power, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: Some 2.0L turbo engines were built with damaged connecting rod bearings. Once a bearing wears through, the engine can seize, and leaking oil could even start a fire.
issues.next: Have a VW dealer check your VIN for the open recalls. If you hear knocking or see an oil pressure light, stop driving and have the car towed. The dealer inspects the engine and replaces it if needed, free of charge.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings that come back after topping up, a sweet smell, or a pink or purple puddle under the middle of the car (2.0T) or under the passenger side of the engine (V6).
issues.why: The water pump seal and housing start to seep as they age. Leaks are most common on the 2.0L turbo but also happen on the 3.6L V6.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and use only VW-approved coolant. If the warning keeps returning, have the pump pressure-tested soon, because running low on coolant can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant warning light, a puddle at the front of the car, and the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: Radiator leaks are the most-reported problem on the 2018 Atlas, usually appearing around 25,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and do not keep driving if the temperature gauge rises. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and ask the dealer about warranty coverage.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The Atlas will not start or cranks slowly after sitting, sometimes on a fairly new battery.
issues.why: Owners of early Atlases report repeated dead batteries. Common causes are modules that stay awake after the car is locked, or a battery that has been run down several times and lost capacity.
issues.next: Have the battery load-tested and a parasitic draw test done. Ask the dealer about software updates for the control modules. Replacement batteries must be registered to the car with a scan tool.

issues.t: Front axle shaft can break
issues.sym: A clunk or bang followed by a loss of drive. The engine revs but the car does not move, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.why: Some 2018 Atlas owners report a front drive axle (CV shaft) breaking at only a few thousand miles.
issues.next: If you hear clicking or clunking when turning or pulling away, have the axles inspected. If drive is lost, do not drive the car; have it towed.

issues.t: Steering rack mounting bolt can corrode and break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk when turning, or steering that feels loose or vague.
issues.why: A mounting bolt for the steering rack can corrode and snap. If it breaks, the rack housing can crack and steering control can be lost.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done right away. If the steering feels loose, stop driving and have the car towed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag can switch off with an adult in the seat (recall)
issues.sym: The "passenger airbag off" light comes on even when an adult is sitting in the front seat.
issues.why: A wiring fault in the seat occupant detection system can make the car think the seat is empty, so the front passenger airbag may not deploy in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-215 and 24V-464. Until it is fixed, watch the passenger airbag light, and have the wiring repaired by a dealer.

issues.t: Door wiring corrosion can delay side airbags (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, often after wet weather.
issues.why: Contacts in the door wiring harness can corrode, which can delay the front side airbags in a side crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Have the door wiring connectors repaired if the airbag light is on.

issues.t: Water from the A/C drain can trigger the airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the passenger side and an airbag warning light.
issues.why: A twisted A/C drain tube can let water drip onto the airbag control module. The water can make airbags go off unexpectedly or not work in a crash.
issues.next: Check for this recall. If you find wet front carpet, have the A/C drain and airbag module checked right away.

issues.t: Blocked A/C drain can leak onto the airbag module (recall)
issues.sym: Water on the front floor and possibly an airbag warning light.
issues.why: The A/C drain can clog and let water reach the airbag control module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-892 and have the drain fixed.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may tear when it deploys (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The passenger airbag could tear or unfold the wrong way in a crash, giving less protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the airbag replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt buckles can be damaged by child seats (recall)
issues.sym: A cracked or loose second-row buckle, or one that is hard to latch.
issues.why: Wide child seat bases can damage the second-row buckles, which might then release in a crash.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the buckles under the recall.

issues.t: Brake caliper pistons may reduce braking (recall)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: Some front brake caliper pistons were made without enough coating, which can reduce braking.
issues.next: This was a do-not-drive recall. Confirm with a dealer that it has been done before driving.

issues.t: Brake caliper bracket bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk when braking or the car pulling to one side.
issues.why: Caliper bracket bolts may not have been tightened enough at the factory, letting the caliper shift.
issues.next: Have the dealer check and torque the bolts under the recall.

issues.t: Rear coil springs can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, one corner sitting lower, or damage to the rear tire sidewall.
issues.why: The rear coil springs can break early. A broken spring end can cut into the tire.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the springs replaced. If one corner sits low, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Factory Continental tires can fail at the sidewall (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge in the tire's sidewall or sudden air loss.
issues.why: Some original Continental tires were over-cured during production and can break at the sidewall or lose tread.
issues.next: Check your tires for bulges and have them checked under the tire recall.

issues.t: Fuel tank can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel dripping near the rear of the car.
issues.why: Some fuel tanks were built with walls that were too thin or with a manufacturing flaw that can cause leaks.
issues.next: Avoid parking in a garage if you smell fuel, and get the recall done quickly.

issues.t: Fuel tank suction jet can leak and cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, or the engine stalling with fuel still in the tank.
issues.why: A suction jet inside the tank was welded in the wrong place, which can cause a leak and poor fuel transfer between the tank halves.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN and have the fuel tank repaired under the recall.

issues.t: Wrong side airbag may be installed (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: The wrong side impact airbag may have been fitted to the driver or passenger seat.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the airbag replaced.

issues.t: Driver side airbag housing may be missing a weld (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: A missing weld on the driver side airbag housing can let it deploy the wrong way or come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the part replaced.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may miss low tires (recall)
issues.sym: No low-tire warning even though all four tires are low.
issues.why: The tire pressure system may not notice when all four tires lose pressure at the same time.
issues.next: Check tire pressures yourself monthly and get the software update.

issues.t: Front steering knuckles can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension or steering that wanders or suddenly feels off.
issues.why: Some steering knuckles were damaged during production and could crack at the strut mount.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the knuckles inspected and replaced.

issues.t: Front seat frame welds may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: The seatback moves or flexes when you lean on it.
issues.why: Welds on the front seat frame and backrest adjuster may be weak and could fail in a rear crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the seat inspected.

issues.t: Damaged relays can run the horn or starter on their own (recall)
issues.sym: The horn sounds or the starter engages unexpectedly, or a burning smell.
issues.why: Damaged relays can switch the horn or starter on by themselves, which can overheat and cause a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the relays replaced quickly.

issues.t: Wheels or wheel bearing bolts may not be secured properly (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, or vibration.
issues.why: Some wheels had incorrectly machined bolt holes, and some front wheel bearing bolts were not tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls and have the wheels and bearings checked.

issues.t: Fuel injectors may leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, rough running or a check engine light.
issues.why: Some long fuel injectors were built without filters and could leak fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the injectors replaced.

issues.t: Backup camera can go black or freeze (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera screen stays black in reverse, or the infotainment screen freezes.
issues.why: Software and memory chip faults in the infotainment system can stop the rear camera image from showing.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look over your shoulder until the recall software or hardware fix is done.

issues.t: Trailer hitch bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: The hitch clunks or moves when towing.
issues.why: Hitch mounting bolts may not have been tightened enough and could loosen.
issues.next: Do not tow until the recall is done.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear or the car pulling or wandering.
issues.why: Driver-side rear trailing arm bolts may loosen and fall out, which could let the arm break.
issues.next: Have the bolts replaced under the recall soon.

issues.t: Brake lines can leak at the fittings (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light, a soft pedal, or fluid near a wheel.
issues.why: Brake lines may leak where they thread together, letting fluid escape.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal feels soft, stop driving and have the car towed. Get the recall done.

issues.t: Chassis and brake bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the chassis, pulling, or vague handling.
issues.why: Some chassis, brake and suspension bolts may not have been tightened correctly at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the bolts checked and torqued.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder may have the wrong part (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light or a pedal that feels different or sinks.
issues.why: An incorrect spring retainer can block a fluid port in the master cylinder and cause loss of braking.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN and have the master cylinder replaced quickly.

issues.t: Engine cover can come loose and melt after service (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell, or the engine cover out of place.
issues.why: After service the engine cover may not be clipped in properly, so it can touch hot parts and melt.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell burning plastic after a service visit, have the cover checked right away.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be delayed, distorted or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The camera picture appears late, looks warped, or does not appear when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Infotainment software errors and low-voltage events can stop or distort the camera image.
issues.next: Get the software updates under the recalls and use your mirrors until then.

issues.t: Transmission may lose drive suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: A transmission warning and sudden loss of power to the wheels.
issues.why: Some transmissions may have been built incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the transmission inspected or replaced.
